issues.title: Fall 2026 capital borrowing package
issues.status: Approved: about $84 million in new borrowing authorized Oct 13 and Oct 27
issues.summary: After accepting an updated capital and debt plan in August, the Board took up 16 borrowing and funding resolutions in the fall. They cover wastewater and sewer work, the landfill, trash equipment, two public pools, fire facilities, library renovation design, a new city finance software system and a new Public Works garage. All passed, most with one or a few no votes.
points: Aug 11: Board accepted the Ad Hoc Joint Committee's updated capital and debt plan (Johnson opposed, Kelly abstained).
Sep 22: Sixteen resolutions (R-26-059 to R-26-074) introduced, with hearings set for Oct 6 and Oct 26.

Oct 13: Approved about $61 million, including $43.5 million for a Public Works garage, $5 million for two pools and about $9.8 million for wastewater and sewer work. Landfill bond R-26-062 tabled 10-3.
Oct 27: Approved $9 million for an ERP system (10-4), $3 million for library design (10-4), $3.5 million for fire facilities (13-1 each) and $5.17 million for equipment (13-1).
Oct 27: Landfill bond R-26-062 ($2 million) taken off the table and passed 11-3. No: Thibeault, Sullivan, Johnson.

members: Matthew Gregg (elected 2023; city page lists term to Dec 31, 2028)

members: Gary Lambert (Vice Chair, term to Dec 31, 2027)

commissions.note: Appointed: three commissioners named by the Governor of New Hampshire through the Governor and Executive Council. Makes rules for the police force, appoints and can remove officers, and controls police buildings. Meets monthly.

boards.name: Planning Board
boards.meets: 1st and 3rd Thursday, 7 PM, City Hall 3rd floor auditorium (one meeting, on the 2nd Thursday, in July, August and December)
boards.does: Reviews site plans, subdivisions and conditional use permits, writes the master plan and recommends zoning changes to the aldermen.

boards.name: Zoning Board of Adjustment
boards.meets: 2nd and 4th Tuesday, 6:30 PM, City Hall 3rd floor auditorium (one meeting in December)
boards.does: Decides variances, special exceptions and appeals of staff zoning decisions.

boards.name: Historic District Commission
boards.does: Approves exterior changes and building permits for properties in the Nashua Historic District.

boards.name: Conservation Commission
boards.does: Reviews projects under the city wetland ordinance and advises the Zoning Board; protects natural and watershed resources.

boards.name: Board of Assessors
boards.does: Responsible for all property assessments in the city and rules on tax abatement requests.

budget.departmentsNote: Nashua's department-level budget lives in the city's ClearGov digital budget book, which could not be read as text. These figures come from news reports of the Mayor's proposals (Nashua Telegraph, April 16, 2025 for FY26 and June 11, 2026 for FY27), the school district's May 2026 presentation to the aldermen, and Budget Review Committee minutes. They are rounded proposal figures, not final adopted department totals, and do not add up to the general fund. The general fund figure is the Mayor's proposed $384,288,315 in R-26-028; the final adopted general fund was about $384 million after a $288,679 technical cut, committee changes, a $404,617 raise for unaffiliated employees and a $10,083 cut (exact adopted figure not found).
drivers: Employee medical benefits up $3.4 million (7.5%); the Mayor's December 2025 budget memo expected a 12% rise in medical benefits.
Special education: contract services up $1.8 million (51.4%) and out-of-district tuition up $1 million (16.1%); school busing up $1.7 million (15.8%).
Non-medical insurance policies and claims up $1.5 million (19.5%), including workers' compensation the city says it cannot cut.
Partly offset by cutting 56 school positions ($2.4 million) and $4.7 million in other cuts, including $2 million from the equipment replacement fund and $1.73 million in salaries.
